newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Soft but upward momentum intact.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Soft but upward momentum intact.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps were quoted lower at midday on Thursday on overnight crude losses but an uptrend is still intact, traders said.
Swaps levels just slipped slightly on lower crude values but the market is still supported by buying interest in the physical market, brokers said.

The Brent June contract settled lower in London on Wednesday at $17.81, breaking the previous supprt of $17.90, due to soft U.S. gasoline demand as well as a build in U.S. crude stocks last week which have sent New York markets diving.
Brokers said May gas oil swaps were quoted at $25.50/25.70 per barrel around Wednesday's quotes at $25.60/25.70
But fuel oil swaps, tracking crude, were lower at $97.50/98.50 per tonne for May, compared to $98.25/98.75 a day earlier.
Brokers said the local trader who had been buying gas oil in recent months has switched his focus to the fuel oil and jet market.
On Wednesday, he was bidding for an early May cargo of fuel oil at $99.00 per tonne, raising his day earlier bid at $97 per tonne.
The physical fuel oil market is also expected to gain strength with reduced South Korean and Kuwaiti exports in May.
The same trader also purchased a jet cargo on Wednesday for early May lifting at $25.60 per barrel from a European major.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade is steady with May quoted notionally at minus 60/45 cents a barrel.
